inspection_summary: Inspected all 918 logical lines of the hash-bound normalized article, including 900 LF-delimited records and 18 form-feed page boundaries. The paper combines smooth convolution identities for zeta and log zeta with a sparse multiplicative resonator. Convolution replaces an awkward pointwise approximation by a band-limited Dirichlet series while isolating the pole or off-critical-zero terms; a divisor-closed, prime-band construction concentrates multiplicative mass; positivity then turns a weighted mean into an extreme-value lower bound. Distinct odd and even kernels select S and S1. The argument is rigorous within its stated hypotheses, but formulas are heavily layout-dependent: roots, iterated logarithms, set operations, Fourier transforms, and long sums are frequently split or decorated by OCR artifacts, so every exact bound and normalization requires PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Smooth convolution avoids the pole term that limits a classical pointwise approximation
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 1 improves the leading constant in the extreme-value lower bound. The source identifies the mechanism precisely: instead of a truncated pointwise approximation whose explicit pole contribution is troublesome on short lower ranges, convolve zeta with a suitable smooth kernel so that the pole becomes harmless for every beta below one.
accepted_units.context_note: The theorem's exact square-root scale and allowed constant depend on beta. Lines 52-62 give the causal explanation for the gain rather than merely announcing a stronger estimate.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The theorem display has split radicals, iterated logarithms, and OCR punctuation. Verify the exact exponent, constant restriction, interval, and approximation (2) against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: S and its primitive isolate the fluctuating remainder in zero counting
accepted_units.why_material: The paper fixes the branch and jump convention for the argument of zeta, places S directly in the Riemann-von Mangoldt formula, and contrasts unconditional and RH-conditional upper and lower bounds. Theorem 2 then states improved conditional extremes for both S and S1 on a movable interval.
accepted_units.context_note: The distinction between absolute maximum for S and positive maximum for S1 is material and later traced to kernel parity and coefficient sign.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the branch convention, half-jump definition, normalization by pi, and exact powers of log, log log, and log log log. Equations (3)-(5) are vertically fragmented and require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: A Cauchy-kernel formula transfers large log-zeta values into lower bounds for the primitive S1
accepted_units.why_material: Starting from a conditional integral representation of log absolute zeta in terms of S, integration by parts replaces S with S1 and an explicit signed kernel. Choosing sigma just to the right of the critical line then imports an earlier large-value result to obtain a preliminary conditional S1 bound.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a weaker precursor to Theorem 2 but exposes a reusable bridge between a function and its primitive rather than serving only as historical context.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires the exact conditional formula, endpoint term, kernel denominator, and sigma choice. The displayed integral is crowded and must be checked against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Longer positive resonators improve amplitude but enlarge the location interval and lose sign flexibility
accepted_units.why_material: The authors contrast resonance with high moments and with earlier shorter resonators. Larger primes and a longer Dirichlet polynomial improve the detectable maximum, but currently yield a much larger interval and no comparable measure estimate. Because all coefficients are nonnegative, the construction detects large positive real parts and cannot symmetrically force both signs.
accepted_units.context_note: The source explicitly presents the missing measure estimate as an impasse and connects it to the inability to make some conditional results unconditional.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Primarily prose-based; exact comparisons to prior quantitative results remain citation-dependent.

accepted_units.title: Contour shifting turns a smoothed zeta value into a weighted Dirichlet series plus an explicit pole residue
accepted_units.why_material: Lemma 1 shifts a contour from the critical strip to an absolutely convergent line, expands zeta there, and shifts each kernel integral back. The result cleanly separates Fourier-selected Dirichlet coefficients from the residue of the zeta pole.
accepted_units.context_note: Analyticity of the kernel in a horizontal strip and quadratic horizontal decay justify the contour and limit operations. This identity is the input that replaces the classical approximation in Theorem 1.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires Fourier-transform convention, kernel shift signs, contour orientation, and pole location. There appears to be a sign/argument layout discrepancy across displayed intermediate formulas; verify equation (6) and its proof against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: The smoothed logarithm equals a prime series plus an explicit correction from zeros to the right
accepted_units.why_material: Selberg's convolution formula writes log zeta as a von-Mangoldt Dirichlet series plus integrals over any zeros with real part beyond sigma. RH removes that correction at the critical line. Taking imaginary parts yields the S formula, while a bounded correction and an extra logarithmic denominator yield the S1 formula.
accepted_units.context_note: This unit makes the source's conditionality transparent: RH is used to delete a named zero term, not hidden inside the resonator. The real-valued-kernel assumption controls the imaginary/real projections.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-sensitive: zero-sum limits, von Mangoldt weights, Fourier coefficients, bounded h(t), and O-terms must be checked in equations (7)-(10). OCR corrupts some hats and parentheses.

accepted_units.title: Prime bands and square-free multiplicative weights build a large but cardinality-controlled resonator
accepted_units.why_material: The resonator uses a multiplicative weight supported on square-free products of primes in carefully chosen logarithmic bands. Removing integers with too many factors in any band produces a divisor-closed set M whose cardinality stays below N while preserving the desired multiplicative structure.
accepted_units.context_note: The parameters gamma and a balance the number and concentration of selected prime factors. Lemma 3 supplies the cardinality gate used when the support is later discretized.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The exact prime window, f(p), thresholds, and set subtraction/union around lines 333-340 are layout-degraded. Prose recovers divisor closure, but all quantitative definitions need PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Exponential tail estimates show that truncation preserves the weighted prime contribution
accepted_units.why_material: Lemma 4 proves a lower bound for a normalized weighted divisor sum. It introduces a narrower typical set, reduces the claim to showing exceptional multiplicative mass is negligible, factorizes each prime band, and chooses an exponential tilt b so the tail exponent is negative.
accepted_units.context_note: The proof of one symmetric exceptional tail is omitted by reference to earlier work; the displayed argument fully exposes the low-tail mechanism and explains why alpha can approach one.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on exact normalization, band thresholds, products over primes, and the sign of b-1-alpha log b. Several set symbols and sums are split; equations (12)-(16) require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Geometric binning compresses the support while preserving near-multiplicative correlations
accepted_units.why_material: The construction chooses one representative from each narrow multiplicative interval and assigns it the square root of nearby f-mass. Gaussian Fourier decay then controls off-diagonal pairs in the L2 norm, while Cauchy-Schwarz transfers exact relations mk=n on M to approximate relations on the thinned set M-prime.
accepted_units.context_note: This compression keeps the resonator length bounded by N and prepares the coefficient sums used in Lemmas 6 and 7.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires exact interval endpoints, neighborhood used in r(m), Gaussian normalization, and tolerance 3/T. Prime marks and intersection notation are OCR-fragile; verify equations (17)-(21).

accepted_units.title: Positivity lets a resonator retain a favorable finite subcollection of any Dirichlet series
accepted_units.why_material: Lemma 6 abstracts the resonance step for an absolutely convergent Dirichlet series with nonnegative coefficients. Expanding the weighted integral makes every term nonnegative, so a selected finite portion indexed by the resonator's multiplicative relations yields an exponential lower bound.
accepted_units.context_note: Uniformity of the little-o term with respect to F is recorded. The omitted final estimate is explicitly delegated to a cited earlier computation, so this source does not independently contain every detail.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the coefficient minimum up to T^epsilon, parameter kappa, and the exact exponential scale. Equation (23) is visually fragmented and requires PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Restricting the von-Mangoldt series to selected primes converts combinatorial divisor mass into the S-scale gain
accepted_units.why_material: Lemma 7 adapts positivity to coefficients Lambda(n)a_n/log n. Keeping only primes in the designated set transforms the weighted integral into the divisor sum controlled by Lemma 4, producing the square-root log T log3 T over log2 T scale.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the bridge from the generic resonator to the prime-weighted convolution formulas for S and S1.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires exact square-root normalization, prime coefficient minimum, and use of Lambda(p)=log p. Equations (24) and the preceding displays are split across lines and need PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: A compact-frequency even kernel combines pole control, interval localization, and positive resonance
accepted_units.why_material: The proof selects a sinc-squared kernel whose Fourier transform is nonnegative and compactly supported. Moment bounds control the central interval, Gaussian decay removes the far tail, kappa below 1-beta suppresses errors, Lemma 1 supplies the positive Dirichlet series, and Lemmas 5-6 convert the weighted mean into the claimed maximum.
accepted_units.context_note: The final rescaling of T and slight adjustment of beta restore the theorem's target interval after the proof first locates a value in an enlarged range.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact kernel scaling, triangular Fourier transform, error powers, interval endpoints, and lower bound for the Fourier coefficient are essential. Equations (25)-(28) require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: An odd kernel turns the imaginary prime series into a lower bound for the absolute size of S
accepted_units.why_material: For S, the proof differentiates a Gaussian to obtain a real odd kernel with purely imaginary Fourier transform. The conditional convolution formula, second-moment localization, and Lemma 7 then select the imaginary part of the prime series and yield a lower bound for max absolute S.
accepted_units.context_note: The paper explicitly identifies oddness as the reason this argument gives an absolute-value result rather than a one-sided positive extreme.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires kernel parity, Fourier phase, the minimum of Im K-hat on the prime band, and all scaling by log2 T. OCR introduces an extra parenthesis in some S integrals; verify equations (29)-(32).

accepted_units.title: An even positive-frequency kernel yields a one-sided positive extreme for S1
accepted_units.why_material: For S1, an even Gaussian kernel has a real positive Fourier transform. The same localization and resonance architecture now extracts the real prime series with an additional log denominator, explaining both the positive sign and the extra powers of log log in the final scale.
accepted_units.context_note: The bounded correction h is absorbed into the error term. The proof reuses Lemma 7 and differs materially from the S case through parity and coefficient normalization.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires exact Gaussian transform, K-hat/log p minimum, V(t) error, and final exponent of log2 T. Verify equations (33)-(34) against the PDF.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Smooth first, then resonate: representation engineering exposes coefficients a positive selector can use
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Convolution transforms zeta observables into Fourier-filtered Dirichlet series while isolating pole or zero corrections; once the remaining coefficients are nonnegative, the resonator can discard unfavorable terms and retain a multiplicatively aligned subcollection.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: For log zeta and the resulting S/S1 formulas, removal of the zero correction is conditional on RH; positivity also prevents symmetric sign selection.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: A useful resonator balances combinatorial mass, cardinality, and Fourier off-diagonal decay
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Prime-band weights create multiplicative gain, exceptional-factor truncation preserves most weighted mass while enforcing a size cap, and geometric thinning compresses the support so Gaussian decay controls off-diagonal frequency interactions.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The parameter balance is specific to the stated logarithmic scale and relies partly on estimates imported from earlier work; it is not an automatic template for arbitrary coefficient systems.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Kernel parity selects both the observable component and the sign information recoverable by resonance
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: A real odd kernel has an imaginary Fourier transform and selects S through the imaginary prime series, yielding only an absolute extreme; a real even kernel has positive real transform and selects a one-sided positive extreme of S1.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This explains the asymmetry of the proved results, not the true sign distribution or optimal order of either function.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Improved amplitude trades against localization and prevalence
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Longer resonators built from larger primes improve the lower-bound scale, while the proof must work on a larger interval and currently gives no comparable estimate for how often the extreme values occur.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source proves existence of a large value only; it explicitly leaves measure estimates and several opposite-sign bounds unresolved.

within_source_saturation: Saturated at the level of distinct mechanisms and limitations. Every proof stage is represented: pole-aware smoothing, RH-visible zero correction, prime-band construction, exceptional-mass control, support thinning, positive resonance, localization, and parity-specific extraction of S and S1. Further splitting would isolate routine inequality propagation or repeated applications of the same weighted-integral template, while references and acknowledgements carry no additional source-local mechanism.
stop_reason: All 918 logical lines were inspected. The omitted mathematical lines are connective transitions or repeated technical propagation within already selected proof mechanisms. Two formula spans whose exact notation is unsafe are explicitly marked extraction-defective, and every formula-sensitive unit requests PDF verification; no quota or arbitrary unit ceiling was used.
